title: Relative Cartesian model structure on marked simplicial sets
statement:
Use the universes, marked simplicial sets, markings $K^\flat,K^\sharp$, marked products and model-category conventions of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and the cartesian and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $S$ be a small simplicial set. An object of $\mathsf M_S$ is a marked simplicial set $X$ with a simplicial map to $S$; maps lie over $S$ and preserve markings. Define
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_S(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf M_S}(X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Y),$$
where the base map of the product ignores the second factor. For a cartesian fibration $q:Z\to S$, let $Z^\natural$ mark exactly its cartesian edges. A Cartesian equivalence $f:X\to Y$ is a map for which $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_S(Y,Z^\natural)\to\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_S(X,Z^\natural)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every small cartesian fibration $Z\to S$.

The category $\mathsf M_S$ has a left proper combinatorial simplicial model structure with monomorphisms as cofibrations and Cartesian equivalences as weak equivalences; its fibrant objects are exactly the $Z^\natural$. Its Kan enrichment is $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_S$, and all objects are cofibrant. For fibrant $X^\natural,Y^\natural$, this enrichment is the core of the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Y)$ on cartesian-edge-preserving functors. A map between these fibrant objects is a weak equivalence if and only if every map of vertex fibers is an equivalence of quasicategories, and if and only if it has a marked inverse over $S$ up to coherent natural equivalences over $S$.

For every simplicial map $a:T\to S$, composition $a_!:\mathsf M_T\to\mathsf M_S$ is left Quillen and its right adjoint is degreewise pullback $a^*$. Pullbacks of cartesian fibrations represent homotopy pullbacks in the Joyal model structure. Taking opposites gives the cocartesian model structure with these assertions and cocartesian edges in place of cartesian edges.
